result: The authors demonstrate that WRN and WRNIP1 ATPase activities do not affect the efficiency of replication fork progression through UV lesions. DNA fiber assays show that RF progression through UV lesions occurs as proficiently in cells defective in WRN ATPase, WRNIP1 ATPase, or both activities (including combined with WRN exonuclease deficiency) as in WT cells. Additionally, the accumulation of WRN or WRNIP1 into UV-induced replication foci was not affected by the K577A and K274A mutations.
evaluation: All reviewers accept these findings without challenge. Reviewer 1 states 'These defects generally do not affect the efficiency of the bypass, only its fidelity.' Reviewer 2 notes 'progression of the replication forks through UV lesions was not affected in cells lacking the WRN exonuclease activity as well as the WRN and WRNIP1 ATPase activities.' The data in Figure 1 are not questioned by any reviewer.

result: Defects in WRN and WRNIP1 ATPase activities cause a dramatic increase in mutation frequencies during TLS through CPDs by Polη. The authors show that defects in WRN ATPase activity increase UV-induced mutation frequency by ~31 × 10⁻⁵, WRNIP1 ATPase defects increase it by ~33 × 10⁻⁵, and combined defects in both ATPases plus WRN exonuclease increase mutation frequency to ~90 × 10⁻⁵. These effects are independent of Polθ, as demonstrated by experiments in Polθ-depleted cells and with the Polθ inhibitor ART558.
evaluation: All reviewers explicitly accept these findings. Reviewer 1 states 'They showed that the ATPase activities of both WRN and WRNIP1, as well as the exonuclease activities of WRN, are necessary high fidelity of Y-family polymerases in cells.' Reviewer 2 notes 'a vast increase in error-prone TLS, notably through CPDs by Polη.' The editor states the manuscript 'provides convincing evidence' for these roles. The mutation frequency data in Table 1 and Figure 2 are not questioned.

result: Defects in WRN and WRNIP1 ATPase activities cause distinct patterns of nucleotide misincorporations opposite CPDs by Polη. WRN ATPase defects primarily increase misinsertion of A or C opposite the C residue of CPD, while WRNIP1 ATPase defects additionally increase misinsertion of C, G, or T opposite the T residue of CPD. These defects also cause mutational hot spot formation in different sequence contexts.
evaluation: Reviewers accept these mutational spectra findings. Reviewer 2 notes 'differential impacts on the nature of mutations between WRN ATPase and WRNIP1 ATPase.' Reviewer 3 states 'the authors examined the generality of their results in terms of TLS pols and DNA lesions.' The mutational spectra data in Figure 3 are described as 'convincing and well supported' by Reviewer 2.

result: Defects in WRN ATPase, WRNIP1 ATPase, and WRN exonuclease activities each increase error-proneness of TLS through (6-4) photoproducts by Polη and Polι to a similar extent, with additive effects. In WT cells, error-prone TLS through (6-4) PPs generates mutations at ~14 × 10⁻⁵, which rises to ~32 × 10⁻⁵ with single activity defects and ~76 × 10⁻⁵ when all three activities are defective (approximately fivefold increase).
evaluation: Reviewers accept these findings without challenge. Reviewer 1 notes the authors 'examined the bypass of 6-4 photoproducts by polymerases eta and iota' and found effects on fidelity. Reviewer 2 states findings are 'convincing and well supported.' The mutation frequency data in Figure 4 are not questioned by any reviewer.

result: Defects in WRN and WRNIP1 ATPase activities elevate specific types of nucleotide misinsertions opposite (6-4) photoproducts. Both ATPases restrain misinsertion of A opposite the C residue of (6-4) PPs, while WRNIP1 ATPase additionally prevents misinsertion of T or G opposite the T residue. These defects also expose misinsertions at UV photoproducts presumably formed at non-dipyrimidine sequences.
evaluation: Reviewers accept the mutational spectra findings for (6-4) PPs. Reviewer 2 notes the authors provide evidence for 'differential impacts on the nature of mutations' and that 'defects in these ATPase activities cause mutational hot spot formation in different sequence contexts.' The data in Figure 5 are described as part of findings that are 'convincing and well supported.'

result: At the thymine glycol (Tg) lesion, WRNIP1 ATPase activity is required for error-free TLS by Polκ, while WRN ATPase has no effect. Defects in WRNIP1 ATPase raise mutation frequency from ~2% to ~9%, primarily from G insertion opposite the 5' T next to Tg. Unexpectedly, an epistatic interaction between WRNIP1 ATPase and WRN exonuclease suggests WRNIP1 ATPase facilitates WRN exonuclease function in removing Polκ misinsertions at this lesion.
evaluation: Reviewers accept these findings. Reviewer 1 states 'they showed that WRNIP1 ATPase defects impair the WRN exonuclease from removing misinsertions by polymerase iota at thymine glycol lesions.' Reviewer 2 notes 'The relative contributions of these activities (exonuclease and ATPase) to the fidelity of TLS Pols, however, vary, depending upon the DNA lesion and the TLS Pol involved.' The data in Table 2 are not questioned.

result: At the εdA lesion, WRN exonuclease plays the dominant role in maintaining fidelity of TLS by Polι, while WRN and WRNIP1 ATPase activities have more modest effects. The exonuclease-deficient E84A WRN mutation elevates mutation frequency from ~19% to ~62%, primarily from C and A misinsertions. Defects in both ATPases elevate G misinsertions by Polι, which are largely removed by WRN exonuclease when it is functional.
evaluation: Reviewers accept these findings. Reviewer 1 notes the authors 'examined the bypass of ethenoadenine by polymerase iota' and found effects on fidelity. Reviewer 2 states 'The relative contributions of these activities (exonuclease and ATPase) to the fidelity of TLS Pols, however, vary, depending upon the DNA lesion and the TLS Pol involved.' The data in Figure 6 are described as part of findings that are 'convincing and well supported.'

result: The authors propose a mechanistic model in which WRN and WRNIP1 ATPase activities restrain nucleotide misincorporations by tightening the active site of TLS polymerases. They suggest that rather than unwinding DNA, the ATPase activities are modified by components of the Y-family Pol multiprotein ensemble to impact the active site of the TLS Pol, limiting misincorporations.
evaluation: Reviewer 1 states 'The authors also discuss a reasonable possibility that complex formation between the WRN and WRNIP1 proteins and Y-family polymerases could tighten the active sites of these polymerases to improve fidelity. Further studies are required to demonstrate this model, but it is a very exciting model that is well supported by the current data.' Reviewer 3 notes 'many readers would be interested in how these ATPases could change molecular structure of Pol eta.' The model is presented as speculation requiring further validation.

result: The combined actions of WRN and WRNIP1 ATPases in preventing nucleotide misincorporations and WRN exonuclease in removing misinserted nucleotides confer an enormous rise in the fidelity of Y-family polymerases, enabling them to perform predominantly error-free TLS. This provides a safeguard against genomic instability and tumorigenesis.
evaluation: All reviewers explicitly support this overarching conclusion. The editor states the manuscript 'provides convincing evidence that WRN and WRNIP1 ATPases, in addition to the previously reported role of the WRN 3'>5' exonuclease activity, are essential for promoting the fidelity of replication through DNA lesions by Y-family Pols in human cells.' Reviewer 1 states 'the conclusions are well supported and convincing.' Reviewer 2 states 'all the findings reported are convincing and well supported' and notes the authors 'identify the means by which these otherwise highly error-prone TLS Pols have been adapted to function in an error-free manner.'
